correctness.rationale: For disjoint edges of a complete multipartite graph, Wang’s connector condition creates a D-conflict exactly when the edges do not lie in the same bipartite cut. Hence the D-conflict graph is the complete join of the line graphs of all cuts. Chromatic number is additive under join, and each cut has chromatic index equal to its maximum side size by the degree lower bound and an explicit cyclic coloring. The maximum-degree corollary follows from a nonnegative algebraic decomposition. The standalone verifier independently reconstructs the definition and exactly checks all multipartite types through seven vertices, with broader construction and bound tests.

value.rationale: D-coloring is a recent edge-coloring invariant whose central conjecture remains open. Complete multipartite graphs form a canonical dense family linking the already-known complete-bipartite and complete-graph endpoints. The theorem gives an exact all-parameter value, identifies the entire conflict graph as a join of line graphs, characterizes the support of every color class, verifies the conjectured bound for an unbounded family, and isolates complete graphs as the equality cases within that family.
